episode_observation.what_happened: Gate-C source-signature auditing found Pineau–Vicol Theorem 1.9 to be a relevant same-domain transformation, but exact direct gluing from the finite-I Albritton–Barker lane fails because three source carriers are not mapped: pointwise Type-I velocity, annular L∞ pressure, and one-time small self-similar-time speed.

diagnoses.statement: Finite I (A+C+D+E) is not the same input type as Pineau–Vicol's pointwise Type-I plus annular pressure carriers.
The one-time generator defect contains ∂t u, equivalently Δu and ∇p after NSE substitution, while finite I has no one-slice Δu/∇p carrier.
The cited finite-I compactness/ancient machinery does not itself state a one-time small ∂sU recurrence/speed conclusion.

scoped_failures.statement: Direct finite-I -> Pineau–Vicol Theorem 1.9 gluing is unlicensed by exact source preconditions.
scoped_failures.scope_limit: Does not rule out a new theorem deriving the missing carriers or applying PV in a stronger Type-I sublane.

scoped_failures.statement: The finite-I ledger has no registered one-slice second-derivative/pressure-gradient carrier for the scaling generator.
scoped_failures.scope_limit: Does not prove non-implication under full NSE dynamics.

reusable_obstruction.statement: A Type-I rigidity route that bypasses generic signed local-energy monotonicity must manufacture a source-valid self-similar-time speed/recurrence defect (and bind any stronger velocity/pressure carriers of its consumer).

lesson_proposal.statement: When importing a one-slice approximate-self-similarity regularity criterion, treat the self-similar-time speed as an independent carrier. Local compactness, scale-critical magnitude budgets, and pressure oscillation do not silently discharge it.
